subject: FinCorp evals: recommended models, dataset format & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinCorp evals: recommended models, dataset format & next steps

Hi Alice —

Great to speak this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and suggested next steps so we can run a focused eval on Redwood: \

1) Goals & constraints (as discussed)
- Primary: high-precision financial Q&A for statements & regulatory language (low hallucination tolerance)
- Latency: 200-2500ms token latency target for interactive UI
- Cost sensitivity: prefer smaller model family if quality is acceptable

2) Recommended model candidates to evaluate (start with A/B):
- redwood-7b-instruct-q4f16 (fast, quantized; good cost/latency tradeoff)
- open-mistral-instruct-7b-v0 (strong few-shot instruction tuning)
- redwood-70b-chat-32k (if you want the highest-quality baseline; heavier footprint)

We typically run a 48-72 hour comparative eval across 1) accuracy on your golden set, 2) semantic-similarity scoring, 3) safety/guardrail checks, and 4) latency/cost metrics.

3) Dataset + prompt set (attached)
- Attached: fincorp_eval_dataset_v1.csv (CSV, header row) — required columns: id, input, expected_output, intent, priority, notes
- Prompt set: included in the CSV as the prompt_template column; we also included negative/edge cases flagged under priority=high
- Format note: prefer UTF-8 CSV, comma-separated, quotes around multi-line fields

4) Scoring & acceptance criteria (draft)
- Automated: exact match where applicable (legal clause extraction), ROUGE/L models for long answers, and semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) threshold >= 0.85 for accept
- Human review: sample of 5% of outputs with a two-rater agreement threshold; any regression >5% triggers investigation

5) How to run this on Redwood (brief)
- Upload dataset to S3 or share the Drive folder above; share read permissions with eval@redwood.com
- I'll spin up a dedicated eval job and provide per-model dashboards (accuracy, latency, per-prompt heatmaps) and raw response CSVs
- We'll enable Redwood Optimize regression alerts tied to this eval set so future model rollouts trigger notifications if performance drops

Next steps I suggest:
- Confirm the attached CSV is the golden set you want us to use (or send an updated file)
- Confirm whether we should include the 70B baseline or only run the 7B class for cost reasons
- Share an S3 path or grant Drive access to eval@redwood.com by EOD Friday
- 30-45 minute kickoff with engineering + security (I'll include Dev Patel to cover technical setup)

I've attached the CSV and a short SOP (redwood-eval-sop.pdf) that has sample manifest examples and scoring config.

Thanks — happy to jump on another call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: FinCorp evals: recommended models, dataset format & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions from our side: \

1) Data retention / privacy: our security team needs to confirm how long the eval artifacts (input + model outputs) are stored and whether they are encrypted at rest. Can you confirm Redwood's default retention policy and encryption standards?

2) Regression detection: you mentioned regression >5% triggers investigation — can Redwood run pairwise comparisons between model versions (baseline vs. variant) and surface the specific prompt buckets where regressions occur? We want to see per-intent breakdowns (ex: "regulatory-extraction" vs "policy-summary").

3) Human-in-the-loop: for edge-case review, can we route low-confidence responses to a small group of reviewers in our org and feed those annotations back into the eval?

Also — we can share an S3 bucket; I'll follow up with the link. Appreciate including Dev for the setup details.

— Alice
Director, Product (NLP) | FinCorp

Subject: Re: FinCorp evals: recommended models, dataset format & next steps

Hi Alice — answers inline below.

1) Data retention / encryption
- Default: Redwood stores eval inputs and outputs for 90 days for hosted eval jobs, encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS available on Dedicated/Private.
- Option: we can configure shorter retention or automatic deletion after the job completes; note that keeping outputs helps reproducibility and model debugging.

2) Regression & per-bucket comparisons
- Yes — Redwood's eval runner produces pairwise diffs and per-bucket breakouts. The dashboard shows delta in accuracy, average embedding distance, and a top-10 list of prompts that drove the regression per intent.
- We can attach the per-intent heatmaps to the HubSpot deal record so you have a single source of truth.

3) Human-in-the-loop
- Supported: we can pipeline low-confidence outputs (below a configurable semantic-similarity threshold) to your reviewers via a Share link or integrate with your annotation tool. Annotations can be uplifted back into the eval as an updated expected_output column for re-runs.

Dev will send the S3 upload guideline and a sample manifest (see his note). For security specifics, Sean will follow up on encryption/KMS options for Dedicated or Private if you need customer-managed keys.

Propose: kickoff tomorrow 10am PT for 30 minutes to confirm S3 path and initial scoring weights — will that work?

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi all — technical bits for the eval upload and manifest. Sample steps below: \

1) Bucket & manifest
- Create an S3 bucket (e.g. fincorp-redwood-evals) and grant read access to: eval@redwood.com and role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-eval-ingest (we will provide the role ARN after kickoff if you prefer cross-account access)
- Manifest format (JSONL or CSV accepted). For CSV use header: id,input,expected_output,prompt_template,priority,intent,metadata

2) Example manifest snippet (CSV)
- id: 001
- input: "Extract the effective date from the attached contract excerpt."
- expected_output: "Effective date: 2024-05-01"
- prompt_template: "Given the document, extract the requested field: {input}"

3) Running the eval (CLI)
- We will provide a one-line CLI runner once we have s3:// path. Example: redwood eval run --manifest s3://fincorp-redwood-evals/manifest.csv --models redwood-7b-instruct-q4f16,open-mistral-instruct-7b-v0 --output s3://fincorp-redwood-evals/results/rdw-4392/ --config scoring.json

4) Scoring config (scoring.json example keys)
- match_type: [exact|semantic|rouge]
- semantic_model: "redwood-embed-2-small"
- semantic_threshold: 0.85
- human_sample_pct: 0.05
- regression_threshold_pct: 5

If you prefer we can also accept the dataset via the Drive link you shared; S3 is just faster for large batches. I've uploaded a sample manifest to the Drive folder for your review.

Let me know when you share the bucket and I'll kick off the job.

— Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
